pr_title: Fixed an issue with sorting items
pr_body:
Fixes #1727 
I fixed it by setting the property `e.Column.SortDirection` to the opposite direction of its previous value.

issue_context.title: List view sorting arrows don't switch right away
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
When changing the sorting order from ascending to descending in any column, the arrow doesn't switch unless you switch from one column to another.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Go to a folder in List view
2. Click on one of the column headers (Name, Status, Type, etc)
3. Switch from ascending to descending. Note the arrow doesn't change.
4. Click the header again and make sure the sort order is opposite the arrow direction (if the arrow is pointing up, make sure the sort order is descending).
5. Click on a different header. The arrow will change direction.

**Expected behavior**
Arrow should change and match direction when header is clicked.

**Screenshots**
![ezgif-4-fc1e4a089212](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8879244/90085926-1c629400-dce7-11ea-97c9-480c02ee9751.gif)

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
 - OS Version: [e.g. Windows 10 2004 20185.1000]
 - App version: [v0.13.0.0]

review_comments: What about to add `e.Column.SortDirection = App.CurrentInstance.FilesystemViewModel.IsSortedAscending ? DataGridSortDirection.Ascending : DataGridSortDirection.Descending;` here instead of your code?
If you switch the sorting column, the previous direction will be used. My code uses `DataGridSortDirection.Ascending` by default.
Ok, then reset sorting by adding `e.Column.SortDirection = DataGridSortDirection.Ascending;` before if statement.
And for future, don't use negation in bool variable names, please.
